\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{पेटवणे} (petavṇe)}{पेटवणे (petavṇe)}]{\mr{पेटवणे} (petavṇe) — to light, to set alight}

\label{lesson:MR-C162-petavne}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for an advert, then the Marathi for a receipt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{पेटवणे}}
\textbf{\mr{पेटवणे}} — \emph{petavṇe} — \textquotedblleft{}to light, to set alight\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
The origin of \textbf{\mr{पेटवणे}} (\emph{petavṇe}) is not settled. Neither CDIAL nor DEDR, searched by form and by meaning, has an entry for it.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{विझवणे} (vijhavṇe)}{विझवणे (vijhavṇe)}]{\mr{विझवणे} (vijhavṇe) — to put out}

\label{lesson:MR-C162-vijhavne}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for a receipt, then the Marathi for to light.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{विझवणे}}
\textbf{\mr{विझवणे}} — \emph{vijhavṇe} — \textquotedblleft{}to put out\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{विझवणे}} (\emph{vijhavṇe}) comes from a reconstructed \emph{*vijjhāpayati}, \textquotedblleft{}extinguishes\textquotedblright{}, the \textquotedblleft{}make\textquotedblright{} form of \emph{*vijjhāyati}, \textquotedblleft{}is extinguished\textquotedblright{}, under which CDIAL lists Marathi \emph{vijhṇẽ} (CDIAL 11703). Bloch derived \emph{vijhṇẽ} from \emph{vi-kṣi} instead.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{उडी} \mr{मारणे} (uḍī mārṇe)}{उडी मारणे (uḍī mārṇe)}]{\mr{उडी} \mr{मारणे} (uḍī mārṇe) — to jump}

\label{lesson:MR-C162-udi-marne}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for to light, then the Marathi for to put out.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{उडी} \mr{मारणे}}
\textbf{\mr{उडी} \mr{मारणे}} — \emph{uḍī mārṇe} — \textquotedblleft{}to jump\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{उडी} \mr{मारणे}} (\emph{uḍī mārṇe}) is \textquotedblleft{}to strike a jump\textquotedblright{}: \emph{uḍī}, \textquotedblleft{}a jump\textquotedblright{}, belongs with \textbf{\mr{उडणे}}, \textquotedblleft{}to fly\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 1697), and \textbf{\mr{मारणे}} comes from Sanskrit \emph{mārayati}, \textquotedblleft{}kills\textquotedblright{}, whose Marathi form CDIAL glosses \textquotedblleft{}to strike, kill\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10066).
\end{cousinweb}
